test_title: PYST 2: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: maths
question: A person marks an article 36% above the cost price and offers 30% discount on the marked price. What is the loss or gain percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the successive percentage change formula: Net % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, x = +36 (Markup) and y = −30 (Discount)

Net Change = 36 − 30 + [36 × (−30)] ÷ 100

Net Change = 6 − 10.8 = −4.8%

The negative sign indicates a loss.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss 4.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 36%

Discount Percentage = 30%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit or Loss % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a961df1fdff05ce8308c35967846a9bb8879011f65dd6fbe511f8d9abfe4cc26.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 36% of 100 = ₹136.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 136 − 30% of 136

⇒ SP = 136 − (30 ÷ 100 × 136)

⇒ SP = 136 − 40.8 = ₹95.2

⇒ Since SP [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the net percentage change is given by [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%.

Relation between CP, MP, Profit, and Discount

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price can be expressed as CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Discount and Profit Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise.
